$comment: Round-trip test fund, 1.3.0 (2026-09-12). A THROWAWAY instance whose only purpose is to run
one full subscribe round trip, one full redeem round trip, and the ADR-027 cancel-while-
accruing path against a real chain -- then be abandoned. It is NOT registered in REXRegistry
(deliberate: the registry keys by rwaToken, which all three 1.3.0 funds share, so registering
this one would make it the version the dApp resolves to). Its config/deployments.json entry
carries "opsDefault": false so `--env sepolia` keeps targeting the operational fund; operate
this one with `tx <verb> --rex-primary <its address>`.
Everything is identical to testnet-dev EXCEPT schedule.epochDuration, which is 300 (5 min, vs
3600) so epoch 1 is triggerable 5 min after the launchpad closes and each later epoch 5 min
after the last -- the accrual path can then be walked repeatedly in one sitting. The EPOCH
clock is the one that needed shortening; the launchpad window did not.
launchpadPeriod STAYS AT 3600. The first attempt set it to 300 and lost the fund: the window
is the only time deposits are accepted (`_requireLaunchpadOpen` bounds them at BOTH ends,
REXPrimary.sol:410), and five minutes does not survive post-deploy wiring plus an approve and
a deposit. A window that closes with less than launchpadMinimum raised leaves exactly one
reachable outcome, LaunchpadFail, which is terminal. Deploy 0xAEf07202 died that way.
WHY THE MINIMUMS STAY AT 20. They are what makes ADR-027 observable at all. A batch only sits
in `Accumulating` -- the one state where the new cancel is legal -- when it is BELOW minSub,
so a fund with minSub 0 (every devnet, and every deploy before 2026-09-09) can never host the
scenario. Deposit less than 20 USDC, let an epoch consume it, and the batch accrues: that is
the state to cancel from. Lowering these to make the round trip easier would delete the
evidence this fund exists to produce.
SC13 §4.2: pruvExecutor.redeemDelay (and minRedeemDelay) must stay below epochDuration - schedule.windowLength.
